title: SCHEMA DOOR: the address-blob format, in one versioned place
supersedes: the format spec embedded in tools/build_libbin.py
why_this_file_exists: The design record (HANDOVER.md section 11) names this as a wanted door and calls the three-way duplication a drift risk: the same format was described in a Python spec, a Python LAYOUT table, and C++ constants. Three descriptions of one format is two descriptions too many, and the risk is not that any of them is wrong, it is that a change lands in two of the three. This file is the single place. The three implementations must conform to it, and tools/spec_lint.py plus the retrieval selftest check that it exists.

provenance.note: Reference implementation of the same idea. NOT a dependency; libxse/addresslib does not exist publicly (404, and the libxse org has no such repo).
HANDOVER.md line 269: (vprobe.addresses.txt / .bin) are the per-build artifacts, and build_libbin.bat selects the per-build file and stages it.

prose: Two artifacts, and the distinction matters. The TEXT form is the human-authored source: mappings named <L1.L2.L3>_<R1.R2.R3>.txt, with a fixed 18-line header that is skipped, then tab-separated pairs of hex offsets. The BINARY form is what ships and what the runtime reads: a bare array with no header, no strings, no version field, no checksum and no magic. That is a deliberate zero-allocation design, and it is why the format is so easy to get subtly wrong. Three traps are recorded below, and all three have already cost somebody time: offsets are RVA not absolute, identifiers are sparse per version, and the count field is never validated before a span is built over it.

artifacts.name: vprobe.addresses.txt
artifacts.notes: The R side is the runtime target. This file is a QUERY, not a fact, until it is compiled into the blob.

artifacts.name: vprobe.addresses.bin

layout.name: count
layout.notes: Number of records that follow. NEVER VALIDATED before a span is built over it; a corrupt or truncated file therefore produces an out-of-range span rather than a clean error.

record.name: id
record.notes: Assigned by union-find over offsets across version pairs, so identical offsets SHARE an id. The counter runs 0..N over GROUPS, which makes ids SPARSE within any one version.

record.name: offset
record.notes: RVA. The image base 0x140000000 is ALREADY SUBTRACTED. Adding it again is the classic error.

invariants: records are sorted ascending by id
no strings, no names, no version field, no checksum, no magic number
the version lives ONLY in the filename
id < count is NOT guaranteed; ids are sparse per version

known_traps.trap: adding the image base a second time
known_traps.consequence: addresses land outside the module, reads fault or return garbage
a lookup for a valid id walks off the end of the array
a truncated file yields a span past end-of-file instead of a clean refusal

known_traps.trap: expecting a version field inside the blob
known_traps.consequence: there is none; read the filename

open_questions: Whether build_libbin.py's LAYOUT and VersionConfig.hpp currently agree with each other, byte for byte, has NOT been verified. This file states the intent; it is not evidence that the three implementations match.
not_established_here: The 18-line header skip count, the exact union-find grouping rule, and the DX10/BA2 name-hash algorithm are not established by this file. The name-hash algorithm is UNDOCUMENTED across four independent BA2 implementations and blocks a correct writer; see ai_context/engine/ba2_format/ba2-format-notes.md.
